baseline.command: source bin/activate-hermit && cargo test -p ponduin --lib coding::
known_gaps: A malformed coding-tool invocation could be recorded as repository activity before parsing succeeded.
The original request was not retained as durable workflow task state for model recovery.
Workflow IDs did not have a distinct runtime type at the tool boundary.
An active coding workflow could reach a generic turn-limit prompt without a retained workflow stop reason.

after.command: source bin/activate-hermit && cargo test -p ponduin --lib coding::

assertions: The exact user request remains available to the recovery instruction.
Recovery does not ask the user to resend the task.
An active workflow suppresses premature final prose.
No process dispatch occurs for invalid parameters.
The malformed request does not create repository-activity evidence.
A tool outside the current workflow contract is rejected before execution.

deterministic_regressions.scenario: rollback ID used where a workflow ID is required
assertions: Only the workflow_<uuid> identifier form deserializes as WorkflowId.
Rollback-shaped identifiers cannot mutate workflow state.
Three equivalent contract failures produce retained diagnostic evidence.
The workflow enters Blocked with RepeatedToolContract rather than claiming success.
A recorded RepeatedToolContract stop reason takes precedence over an unrelated action-limit message.

deterministic_regressions.scenario: empty or premature model completion during an active workflow
assertions: The premature provider prose stays hidden from the user.
The original user request remains persisted.
The final message does not request user resubmission.
The flat Qwen contract creates the same validated requirements, validation command, and rollback strategy as the full contract.
No JSON string is accepted as a structured standard plan.

deterministic_regressions.scenario: native Qwen phase gates and read compatibility
assertions: After workflow start, native Qwen receives only plan and status tools until the plan gate passes.
The documented relative_path read alias resolves through the same bounded file reader.

selected_real_qwen_runs.workspace_policy: isolated temporary Rust fixture; later runs use a committed red Git baseline and no repository source file

observed: The model made malformed coding-tool calls.
No fixture change or successful validation was obtained.
The run ended with the former generic continuation prompt.
The model started a real workflow.
Three equivalent invalid workflow-ID calls were rejected.
The workflow retained RepeatedToolContract evidence and blocked without mutating the fixture.
This run exposed a reporting-priority defect that the terminal-report regression test now covers.
After approximately four minutes there was no tool progress, workspace change, or test execution.
The client was stopped with SIGTERM after process sampling confirmed an idle wait.
The original failing test remained failing; no success was claimed.
qwen3.5:9b exercised workflow creation, malformed nested plans, unsupported fields, guessed paths, and unregistered tools; every invalid request was rejected before mutation.
The compact adapter and phase visibility were refined from those concrete transcripts and covered by deterministic tests.
qwen3:8b also created the real workflow but produced no subsequent tool call within the bounded live window.
The original red fixture remained unchanged and no live run was reported as a repair success.

aggregate.conclusion: The selected real runs prove fail-closed behavior and expose live-model latency, tool-transport, and progress limits. They do not yet prove autonomous repair success for either tested local Qwen model.

release_blockers: No selected real Qwen repair run has reached verified success.
The requested desktop workflow-progress surface is intentionally not implemented yet.
The final desktop build, smoke test, and controlled /Applications replacement have not been performed.
